input.quote: 12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 binds only the Customer and fails the fallback on every material term: it is one-sided rather than mutual, runs eighteen months rather than twelve, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term rather than only personnel directly involved in the Services, contains no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out, and — by barring Customer from "engaging" such persons — is an outright no-hire, which is walk-away territory under the rule. It also conflicts with Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no no-hire commitment and is free to hire anyone responding to general recruitment. Because the parties have evidently bargained for some restriction, we narrow to the fallback (mutual, 12 months from the end of involvement, services personnel only, with advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire) rather than deleting the clause outright.

ops.oldText: 12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
ops.newText: 12.4 For twelve months after the end of a person's involvement in the Services, neither party will knowingly solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in performing or receiving the Services. This Section 12.4 does not restrict either party from (a) placing or responding to general advertisements or recruitment campaigns not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, or (b) hiring or engaging any person who approaches it on an unsolicited basis or who responds to such general advertising or recruitment, and neither party is subject to any no-hire obligation.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have made this restriction mutual and narrowed it to a 12-month non-solicitation of personnel directly involved in the Services, with the customary carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches. We cannot accept a no-hire ("or engage") covering everyone employed by Vendor at any time during the term, which also conflicts with the general-recruitment freedom preserved in Section 12.3.
proposal.summary: Narrow one-sided 18-month no-hire to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs
